title: Regional Council approves 2026 budget
subtitle: Police budgets, transit changes, women's warming centre, library reimbursement, and a contested vote correction dominated the special meeting.
overview: Regional Council met in a special session to consider the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee's final 2026 budget recommendations. The main package, which includes the 2026 operating and capital budgets, passed {{vote:m1}}. It removes the planned expansion of fare inspectors onto GRT buses, adds a pilot of discounted EasyGO 2-Fare cards for community agencies, and funds a free-transit-day pilot for seniors. It also funds a new Kiwanis Transit bus, a 20-bed women's overnight warming centre in Cambridge, and $100,000 in annual funding for the Waterloo Regional Heritage Foundation.

Council voted separately on the Waterloo Regional Police Service budgets. The operating budget passed {{vote:m2}}. The capital budget was first defeated, then recorded as approved {{vote:m3}} after a councillor said the earlier vote had been made in error and it was corrected.

Several councillors objected to how the change was handled and raised concerns about the process. The confirming by-law passed {{vote:m4}}. For residents, the meeting finalizes 2026 service levels, fees and the property tax levy.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2026 operating budget with a property tax levy of $887,328,641, the 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 forecast, and the accompanying fees and charges by-law.
The proposed expansion of fare inspectors onto GRT buses was removed from the 2026 budget, with staffing, revenue and expenses adjusted.
Staff were directed to include $176,000 in the 2026 budget for a 20-bed women's overnight warming centre in Cambridge, rising to $440,000 in the 2027 base budget.
Taxi coupon prices stay at $30 per $60 value with free delivery, funded from the accessibility reserve, and the rideshare accessibility fee rises to $0.15 per trip.
Council approved a pilot of free GRT travel one day a week for residents 65 and older and a pilot of discounted EasyGO 2-Fare cards for non-profit agencies.
Planning and development fees are frozen at 2025 levels pending a new fee framework, and an unfunded Elmira bypass placeholder was added to the capital forecast for 2030.
Council approved the Waterloo Regional Police Service 2026 operating budget with a net expenditure of $298,951,621 and a levy of $272,610,413.
Council approved the police 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 forecast after an earlier vote was corrected.

debate: Several councillors said allowing a colleague to change a vote after the police capital budget was defeated undermined the democratic process. One called it a mockery of democracy and another said it looked like vote maneuvering.

Staff explained that Council has allowed votes to be corrected when made in error, citing an earlier correction that day. The procedure by-law has no provision for changing votes. It does allow a motion to reconsider, which needs notice unless two-thirds of Council waive it.
One councillor questioned whether the wording used was a correction of an error or a change of intent. The councillor in question said the original intent was to vote in favour, as at committee.
Some councillors also noted that another police board member joined online after the capital vote failed, and said the timing concerned them.
A councillor asked whether voting against the confirming by-law would register disagreement with the vote change. The clerk said it would be recorded only as opposition to the by-law.
